sanskrit: yeṣv ahaḥsu tava brahman salilecchā bhaviṣyati tadā marau bhaviṣyanti jalapūrṇāḥ payodharāḥ
english: "On whatever days you shall feel a longing for water, O brāhmaṇa, on those days the rain-clouds in the desert shall become laden with water.

sanskrit: rasavac ca pradāsyanti te toyaṃ bhṛgunandana uttaṅkameghā ity uktāḥ khyātiṃ yāsyanti cāpi te
english: And they shall yield you sweet, savory water, O delight of the Bhṛgus; named 'the clouds of Uttaṅka,' they shall come to be renowned."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ prītimān vipraḥ kṛṣṇena sa babhūva ha adyāpy uttaṅkameghāś ca marau varṣanti bhārata
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, the brāhmaṇa was filled with delight; and even today, O Bhārata, the clouds of Uttaṅka rain down upon the desert.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca uttaṅkaḥ kena tapasā saṃyuktaḥ sumahātapāḥ yaḥ śāpaṃ dātukāmo 'bhūd viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave
english: Janamejaya said: With what austerity was Uttaṅka endowed, that great ascetic of mighty penance, who was minded to lay a curse upon Viṣṇu, the all-powerful?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uttaṅko mahatā yuktas tapasā janamejaya gurubhaktaḥ sa tejasvī nānyaṃ kaṃ cid apūjayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Uttaṅka was endowed with great austerity, O Janamejaya; devoted to his teacher, that radiant one revered no other being at all.

sanskrit: sarveṣām ṛṣiputrāṇām eṣa cāsīn manorathaḥ auttaṅkīṃ guruvṛttiṃ vai prāpnuyām iti bhārata
english: And this was the heart's desire of all the sages' sons, O Bhārata: 'May I attain such service to the teacher as is Uttaṅka's.'

sanskrit: gautamasya tu śiṣyāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ janamejaya uttaṅke 'bhyadhikā prītiḥ snehaś caivābhavat tadā
english: But among the many disciples of Gautama, O Janamejaya, it was for Uttaṅka that the greatest affection and tenderness then arose.

sanskrit: sa tasya damaśaucābhyāṃ vikrāntena ca karmaṇā samyak caivopacāreṇa gautamaḥ prītimān abhūt
english: By his self-restraint and purity, by his vigorous toil, and by his perfect attendance, Gautama was made well pleased with him.

sanskrit: atha śiṣyasahasrāṇi samanujñāya gautamaḥ uttaṅkaṃ parayā prītyā nābhyanujñātum aicchata
english: Now Gautama, having given leave to his thousands of disciples, out of his supreme affection did not wish to grant leave to Uttaṅka.

sanskrit: taṃ krameṇa jarā tāta pratipede mahāmunim na cānvabudhyata tadā sa munir guruvatsalaḥ
english: Old age, my son, by degrees came upon that great sage, yet the sage, fond of his teacher, did not at that time perceive it.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid rājendra kāṣṭhāny ānayituṃ yayau uttaṅkaḥ kāṣṭhabhāraṃ ca mahāntaṃ samupānayat
english: Then once, O lord of kings, Uttaṅka went forth to fetch firewood, and he brought back a great load of wood.

sanskrit: sa tu bhārābhibhūtātmā kāṣṭhabhāram ariṃdama niṣpipeṣa kṣitau rājan pariśrānto bubhukṣitaḥ
english: But overwhelmed by the burden, O subduer of foes, weary and famished, he flung the load of wood down upon the ground, O king.

sanskrit: tasya kāṣṭhe vilagnābhūj jaṭā rūpyasamaprabhā tataḥ kāṣṭhaiḥ saha tadā papāta dharaṇītale
english: A matted lock of his hair, bright as silver, had caught upon the wood, and so it fell along with the firewood onto the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhāraniṣpiṣṭaḥ kṣudhāviṣṭaś ca bhārgavaḥ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ vayaso 'vasthāṃ rurodārtasvaraṃ tadā
english: Then the descendant of Bhṛgu, crushed by the burden and seized by hunger, beholding that condition of his years, wept aloud in anguish.

sanskrit: tato gurusutā tasya padmapatranibhekṣaṇā jagrāhāśrūṇi suśroṇī kareṇa pṛthulocanā pitur niyogād dharmajñā śirasāvanatā tadā
english: Then the teacher's daughter, whose eyes were like lotus-petals, fair-hipped and large-eyed, knowing the law, at her father's command and with bowed head, caught his tears in her hand.

sanskrit: tasyā nipetatur dagdhau karau tair aśrubindubhiḥ na hi tān aśrupātān vai śaktā dhārayituṃ mahī
english: Her two hands were scorched by those drops of tears as they fell; for not even the earth was able to bear those falling tears.

sanskrit: gautamas tv abravīd vipram uttaṅkaṃ prītamānasaḥ kasmāt tāta tavādyeha śokottaram idaṃ manaḥ sa svairaṃ brūhi viprarṣe śrotum icchāmi te vacaḥ
english: Then Gautama, his heart kindly disposed, said to the brāhmaṇa Uttaṅka: "Why, my son, is your mind today so overcome with grief? Speak freely, O brāhmaṇa-sage; I wish to hear your words."

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca bhavadgatena manasā bhavatpriyacikīrṣayā bhavadbhaktigateneha bhavadbhāvānugena ca
english: Uttaṅka said: With my mind fixed upon you, with the wish to do what pleases you, devoted here to you and following your every disposition—

sanskrit: jareyaṃ nāvabuddhā me nābhijñātaṃ sukhaṃ ca me śatavarṣoṣitaṃ hi tvaṃ na mām abhyanujānathāḥ
english: this old age of mine I never perceived, nor did I ever know pleasure; for a hundred years I have dwelt here, yet you did not grant me leave to depart.

sanskrit: bhavatā hy abhyanujñātāḥ śiṣyāḥ pratyavarā mayā upapannā dvijaśreṣṭha śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: For by you, O best of the twice-born, disciples lesser than I, by the hundreds and by the thousands, were granted leave and set forth duly equipped.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca tvatprītiyuktena mayā guruśuśrūṣayā tava vyatikrāman mahān kālo nāvabuddho dvijarṣabha
english: Gautama said: Bound by my affection for you, and by your service to your teacher, a great span of time slipped by unperceived by me, O bull among the twice-born.

sanskrit: kiṃ tv adya yadi te śraddhā gamanaṃ prati bhārgava anujñāṃ gṛhya mattas tvaṃ gṛhān gacchasva mā ciram
english: But if today you have a mind to depart, O descendant of Bhṛgu, then take your leave from me and go home; do not delay.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca gurvarthaṃ kaṃ prayacchāmi brūhi tvaṃ dvijasattama tam upākṛtya gaccheyam anujñātas tvayā vibho
english: Uttaṅka said: What fee for the teacher shall I render? Tell me, O best of the twice-born; having presented it, I would go, granted leave by you, O mighty one.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca dakṣiṇā paritoṣo vai gurūṇāṃ sadbhir ucyate tava hy ācarato brahmaṃs tuṣṭo 'haṃ vai na saṃśayaḥ
english: Gautama said: The satisfaction of teachers is itself the fee, so the good declare; and at your conduct, O brāhmaṇa, I am content, there is no doubt of it.

sanskrit: itthaṃ ca parituṣṭaṃ māṃ vijānīhi bhṛgūdvaha yuvā ṣoḍaśavarṣo hi yad adya bhavitā bhavān
english: And know me to be so well content, O scion of Bhṛgu, that this very day you shall become young, a youth of sixteen years.

sanskrit: dadāmi patnīṃ kanyāṃ ca svāṃ te duhitaraṃ dvija etām ṛte hi nānyā vai tvattejo 'rhati sevitum
english: I give you as wife my own maiden daughter, O twice-born; for none other but she is fit to attend upon your splendor.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ pratijagrāha yuvā bhūtvā yaśasvinīm guruṇā cābhyanujñāto gurupatnīm athābravīt
english: Then, having become young, he accepted that illustrious maiden; and, granted leave by his teacher, he spoke to his teacher's wife:

sanskrit: kiṃ bhavatyai prayacchāmi gurvarthaṃ viniyuṅkṣva mām priyaṃ hi tava kāṅkṣāmi prāṇair api dhanair api
english: "What shall I render to you? Appoint me to a teacher's-fee task; for I long to do what pleases you, even at the cost of my life and my wealth."

sanskrit: yad durlabhaṃ hi loke 'smin ratnam atyadbhutaṃ bhavet tad ānayeyaṃ tapasā na hi me 'trāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: "Whatever jewel in this world is hard to win and most wondrous, that would I bring by my austerity; of this I have no doubt."

sanskrit: ahalyovāca parituṣṭāsmi te putra nityaṃ bhagavatā saha paryāptaye tad bhadraṃ te gaccha tāta yathecchakam
english: Ahalyā said: I am ever well content with you, my son, together with the venerable one; let that suffice. Blessings on you; go, my child, as you wish.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uttaṅkas tu mahārāja punar evābravīd vacaḥ ājñāpayasva māṃ mātaḥ kartavyaṃ hi priyaṃ tava
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But Uttaṅka, O great king, spoke yet again these words: "Command me, O mother; for there is a service of mine that should please you."

sanskrit: ahalyovāca saudāsapatnyā vidite divye vai maṇikuṇḍale te samānaya bhadraṃ te gurvarthaḥ sukṛto bhavet
english: Ahalyā said: The celestial jeweled earrings, well known to be the wife of Saudāsa's—bring those to me; blessings on you, and so the teacher's-fee will be well performed.

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratiśrutya jagāma janamejaya gurupatnīpriyārthaṃ vai te samānayituṃ tadā
english: Promising "So be it," he set forth, O Janamejaya, to fetch those earrings then, for the pleasure of his teacher's wife.

sanskrit: sa jagāma tataḥ śīghram uttaṅko brāhmaṇarṣabhaḥ saudāsaṃ puruṣādaṃ vai bhikṣituṃ maṇikuṇḍale
english: Then Uttaṅka, that bull among brāhmaṇas, went swiftly forth to beg the jeweled earrings of Saudāsa the man-eater.

sanskrit: gautamas tv abravīt patnīm uttaṅko nādya dṛśyate iti pṛṣṭā tam ācaṣṭa kuṇḍalārthaṃ gataṃ tu vai
english: But Gautama said to his wife: "Uttaṅka is not to be seen today." Thus questioned, she told him that he had gone for the sake of the earrings.

sanskrit: tataḥ provāca patnīṃ sa na te samyag idaṃ kṛtam śaptaḥ sa pārthivo nūnaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ vadhiṣyati
english: Then he said to his wife: "This was not rightly done by you; that king, being under a curse, will surely slay the brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: ahalyovāca ajānantyā niyuktaḥ sa bhagavan brāhmaṇo 'dya me bhavatprasādān na bhayaṃ kiṃ cit tasya bhaviṣyati
english: Ahalyā said: It was unknowingly that I appointed the brāhmaṇa to this, O venerable one; yet through your grace no harm at all shall come to him.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ prāha tāṃ patnīm evam astv iti gautamaḥ uttaṅko 'pi vane śūnye rājānaṃ taṃ dadarśa ha
english: Thus addressed, Gautama said to his wife, "So be it." And Uttaṅka, meanwhile, beheld that king in a lonely forest.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtaṃ rājānaṃ ghoradarśanam dīrghaśmaśrudharaṃ nṝṇāṃ śoṇitena samukṣitam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Beholding that king in such a state, dreadful to look upon, wearing a long beard and drenched with the blood of men,

sanskrit: cakāra na vyathāṃ vipro rājā tv enam athābravīt pratyutthāya mahātejā bhayakartā yamopamaḥ
english: the brāhmaṇa felt no fear; but the king, mighty in splendor, a striker of terror, like Yama himself, rose up and addressed him:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvam asi kalyāṇa ṣaṣṭhe kāle mamāntikam bhakṣaṃ mṛgayamāṇasya saṃprāpto dvijasattama
english: "By good fortune, auspicious one, you have come into my presence at the sixth hour, while I was seeking food, O best of the twice-born—as my food."

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca rājan gurvarthinaṃ viddhi carantaṃ mām ihāgatam na ca gurvartham udyuktaṃ hiṃsyam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Uttaṅka said: O king, know me to be one come hither while engaged on a teacher's errand; and the wise declare that one bound on a teacher's errand must not be harmed.

sanskrit: rājovāca ṣaṣṭhe kāle mamāhāro vihito dvijasattama na ca śakyaḥ samutsraṣṭuṃ kṣudhitena mayādya vai
english: The king said: At the sixth hour my meal is ordained, O best of the twice-born, and it cannot be relinquished by me today, hungry as I am.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca evam astu mahārāja samayaḥ kriyatāṃ tu me gurvartham abhinirvartya punar eṣyāmi te vaśam
english: Uttaṅka said: So be it, O great king; but let a compact be made with me. Having accomplished the teacher's errand, I shall return into your power.

sanskrit: saṃśrutaś ca mayā yo 'rtho gurave rājasattama tvadadhīnaḥ sa rājendra taṃ tvā bhikṣe nareśvara
english: And the object I have promised to my teacher, O best of kings, depends upon you, O lord of kings; for that I beg of you, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: dadāsi vipramukhyebhyas tvaṃ hi ratnāni sarvaśaḥ dātā tvaṃ ca naravyāghra pātrabhūtaḥ kṣitāv iha pātraṃ pratigrahe cāpi viddhi māṃ nṛpasattama
english: For you bestow jewels of every kind upon the foremost of brāhmaṇas; you are a giver, O tiger among men, a worthy vessel of giving here on earth—and know me too to be a worthy vessel for receiving, O best of kings.

sanskrit: upākṛtya guror arthaṃ tvadāyattam ariṃdama samayeneha rājendra punar eṣyāmi te vaśam
english: Having presented to my teacher the object that depends on you, O subduer of foes, by this compact, O lord of kings, I shall return into your power.

sanskrit: satyaṃ te pratijānāmi nātra mithyāsti kiṃ cana anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me svaireṣv api kuto 'nyathā
english: Truly do I promise you this; herein there is no falsehood at all. Never before have I spoken untruth even in jest—how then otherwise?

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca yadi mattas tvadāyatto gurvarthaḥ kṛta eva saḥ yadi cāsmi pratigrāhyaḥ sāṃprataṃ tad bravīhi me
english: Saudāsa said: If the teacher's errand that depends on you rests with me, then it is as good as done. And if I am one fit to be received from, tell me now what it is.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca pratigrāhyo mato me tvaṃ sadaiva puruṣarṣabha so 'haṃ tvām anusaṃprāpto bhikṣituṃ maṇikuṇḍale
english: Uttaṅka said: You are ever deemed by me fit to receive from, O bull among men; and so I have come to you to beg the jeweled earrings.

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca patnyās te mama viprarṣe rucire maṇikuṇḍale varayārthaṃ tvam anyaṃ vai taṃ te dāsyāmi suvrata
english: Saudāsa said: The lovely jeweled earrings, O brāhmaṇa-sage, are my wife's; choose some other object, and that I shall give you, O man of good vows.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca alaṃ te vyapadeśena pramāṇaṃ yadi te vayam prayaccha kuṇḍale me tvaṃ satyavāg bhava pārthiva
english: Uttaṅka said: Enough of your evasions! If we are of any worth in your eyes, give me the earrings, and be a man of your word, O king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktas tv abravīd rājā tam uttaṅkaṃ punar vacaḥ gaccha madvacanād devīṃ brūhi dehīti sattama
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the king spoke again to Uttaṅka these words: "Go, O excellent one, and at my word say to the queen, 'Give them.'

sanskrit: saivam uktā tvayā nūnaṃ madvākyena śucismitā pradāsyati dvijaśreṣṭha kuṇḍale te na saṃśayaḥ
english: She, addressed by you with my words, that lady of bright smile, will surely give you the earrings, O best of the twice-born; of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca kva patnī bhavataḥ śakyā mayā draṣṭuṃ nareśvara svayaṃ vāpi bhavān patnīṃ kimarthaṃ nopasarpati
english: Uttaṅka said: Where can your wife be seen by me, O ruler of men? Or why do you not yourself go to your wife?

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca drakṣyate tāṃ bhavān adya kasmiṃś cid vananirjhare ṣaṣṭhe kāle na hi mayā sā śakyā draṣṭum adya vai
english: Saudāsa said: You shall see her today at some forest-stream; for at the sixth hour she cannot be looked upon by me today.

sanskrit: uttaṅkas tu tathoktaḥ sa jagāma bharatarṣabha madayantīṃ ca dṛṣṭvā so 'jñāpayat svaṃ prayojanam
english: Uttaṅka, thus addressed, went forth, O bull of the Bhāratas; and beholding Madayantī, he made known his errand.

sanskrit: saudāsavacanaṃ śrutvā tataḥ sā pṛthulocanā pratyuvāca mahābuddhim uttaṅkaṃ janamejaya
english: Hearing the message of Saudāsa, that large-eyed lady then made reply to the deeply wise Uttaṅka, O Janamejaya:

sanskrit: evam etan mahābrahman nānṛtaṃ vadase 'nagha abhijñānaṃ tu kiṃ cit tvaṃ samānetum ihārhasi
english: "So it is, O great brāhmaṇa; you speak no untruth, O sinless one. But you must bring some token of recognition hither.

sanskrit: ime hi divye maṇikuṇḍale me; devāś ca yakṣāś ca mahoragāś ca tais tair upāyaiḥ parihartukāmāś; chidreṣu nityaṃ paritarkayanti
english: For these celestial jeweled earrings of mine—gods and yakṣas and great serpents alike, eager to carry them off by every kind of stratagem, ever scheme to seize their unguarded moments.

sanskrit: nikṣiptam etad bhuvi pannagās tu; ratnaṃ samāsādya parāmṛṣeyuḥ yakṣās tathocchiṣṭadhṛtaṃ surāś ca; nidrāvaśaṃ tvā paridharṣayeyuḥ
english: Should this jewel be set down upon the ground, the serpents would come and bear it away; should it be worn while one is unclean, the yakṣas would; and should you fall under the sway of sleep, the gods would assail you.

sanskrit: chidreṣv eteṣu hi sadā hy adhṛṣyeṣu dvijarṣabha devarākṣasanāgānām apramattena dhāryate
english: Against all these openings, otherwise unassailable, O bull among the twice-born, it must be borne with vigilance, safe from gods, rākṣasas, and serpents.

sanskrit: syandete hi divā rukmaṃ rātrau ca dvijasattama naktaṃ nakṣatratārāṇāṃ prabhām ākṣipya vartate
english: By day they ooze gold, O best of the twice-born, and by night as well; at night they shine, outshining the radiance of the constellations and stars.

sanskrit: ete hy āmucya bhagavan kṣutpipāsābhayaṃ kutaḥ viṣāgniśvāpadebhyaś ca bhayaṃ jātu na vidyate
english: For one who wears these, O reverend one, whence comes any fear of hunger or thirst? Nor is there ever any fear from poison, fire, or wild beasts.

sanskrit: hrasvena caite āmukte bhavato hrasvake tadā anurūpeṇa cāmukte tatpramāṇe hi jāyataḥ
english: When worn by one who is small, these too become small to fit, and when worn by one of proportionate size, they grow to that measure.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhe mamaite vai kuṇḍale paramārcite triṣu lokeṣu vikhyāte tad abhijñānam ānaya
english: Of such a kind are these earrings of mine, most highly prized, renowned throughout the three worlds. Therefore bring the token of recognition."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa mitrasaham āsādya tv abhijñānam ayācata tasmai dadāv abhijñānaṃ sa cekṣvākuvaras tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Approaching Mitrasaha, he asked for the token of recognition; and that best of the Ikṣvākus thereupon gave him the token.

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca na caivaiṣā gatiḥ kṣemyā na cānyā vidyate gatiḥ etan me matam ājñāya prayaccha maṇikuṇḍale
english: Saudāsa said: This course is not a safe one, yet no other course exists. Knowing this to be my judgment, give him the jeweled earrings.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktas tām uttaṅkas tu bhartur vākyam athābravīt śrutvā ca sā tataḥ prādāt tasmai te maṇikuṇḍale
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Uttaṅka repeated to her the husband's words; and hearing them, she then gave him those jeweled earrings.

sanskrit: avāpya kuṇḍale te tu rājānaṃ punar abravīt kim etad guhyavacanaṃ śrotum icchāmi pārthiva
english: Having obtained the earrings, he spoke again to the king: "What was that secret message? I wish to hear it, O king."

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca prajā nisargād viprān vai kṣatriyāḥ pūjayanti ha viprebhyaś cāpi bahavo doṣāḥ prādurbhavanti naḥ
english: Saudāsa said: By their very nature the kṣatriyas among men honor the brāhmaṇas; yet from the brāhmaṇas many misfortunes also arise for us.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ dvijebhyaḥ praṇato viprād doṣam avāptavān gatim anyāṃ na paśyāmi madayantīsahāyavān svargadvārasya gamane sthāne ceha dvijottama
english: Bowed down before the twice-born though I was, I came to ruin through a brāhmaṇa; and I see no other path, with Madayantī as my helpmate, for reaching heaven's gate or for abiding here, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: na hi rājñā viśeṣeṇa viruddhena dvijātibhiḥ śakyaṃ nṛloke saṃsthātuṃ pretya vā sukham edhitum
english: For a king, above all, who is at odds with the twice-born is unable to abide in the world of men, or to prosper in happiness after death.

sanskrit: tad iṣṭe te mayaivaite datte sve maṇikuṇḍale yaḥ kṛtas te 'dya samayaḥ saphalaṃ taṃ kuruṣva me
english: Therefore at your wish these very earrings of ours have been given by me; now make fruitful for me the compact that you made with me today.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca rājaṃs tatheha kartāsmi punar eṣyāmi te vaśam praśnaṃ tu kaṃ cit praṣṭuṃ tvāṃ vyavasiṣye paraṃtapa
english: Uttaṅka said: O king, so shall I do; I shall return into your power. But I am resolved to put a certain question to you, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca brūhi vipra yathākāmaṃ prativaktāsmi te vacaḥ chettāsmi saṃśayaṃ te 'dya na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: Saudāsa said: Speak, O brāhmaṇa, as you please; I shall give you an answer. I shall today resolve your doubt; herein I have no hesitation.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca prāhur vāksaṃgataṃ mitraṃ dharmanaipuṇyadarśinaḥ mitreṣu yaś ca viṣamaḥ stena ity eva taṃ viduḥ
english: Uttaṅka said: Those who discern the niceties of the law declare a friend to be one true in word; and whoever is false toward his friends, him they know to be a thief.

sanskrit: sa bhavān mitratām adya saṃprāpto mama pārthiva sa me buddhiṃ prayacchasva samāṃ buddhimatāṃ vara
english: You, sir, have today come into friendship with me, O king; therefore grant me even-tempered counsel, O best of the wise.

sanskrit: avāptārtho 'ham adyeha bhavāṃś ca puruṣādakaḥ bhavatsakāśam āgantuṃ kṣamaṃ mama na veti vā
english: I have today attained my object, and you are a devourer of men. Tell me whether it is fitting or not for me to return into your presence.

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca kṣamaṃ ced iha vaktavyaṃ mayā dvijavarottama matsamīpaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha nāgantavyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Saudāsa said: If it is fitting that I should speak here, O most excellent of the twice-born, then, O best of brāhmaṇas, you should by no means come into my presence at all.
